item.title: Version 1.4.1
item.description:
What's New

  • The welcome note is up to date. Flotnote's built-in "Welcome to Flotnote" note now covers the v1.4.0 additions — wiki-links, backlinks, tags, and multiple windows — along with their shortcuts (open in a new window, back and forward, open a file) and folder-view keyboard navigation. It appears on a fresh install; your existing notes are left untouched.

Bug Fixes

  • Hiding the notes window returns you to what you were doing. Summon Flotnote over another app, hide it again, and focus now lands back on that app instead of leaving no app in front. Same when you close the last window.

item.title: Version 1.4.0
item.description:
Flotnote grows a small web of connected notes: link them, see what links back, tag them, and open several at once — while everything stays plain Markdown on your disk.

New Features

  • Open notes in their own windows. Any note can open in its own floating window — Shift+Cmd+N, Cmd-click a note in Browse Notes, or Cmd-click a wiki-link. Cycle between them with Cmd+Opt+backtick, and the window you land on flashes your accent color so you never lose track of it. The show/hide hotkey now treats every Flotnote window as one group: one press hides them all, the next brings back exactly the set you had and focuses the one you used last.
  • Link notes together with wiki-links. Type two square brackets and a picker opens — the same search as Browse Notes — to link an existing note or create a new one on the spot. Links render inline with a flat arrow so they read differently from web links, dim when the note doesn't exist yet, and Cmd-click opens the target in a new window. Cmd+[ and Cmd+] walk back and forward through the notes you followed, like a browser.
  • Backlinks — see what links here. A Linked mentions view lists every note that points at the one you're reading, grouped by file into collapsible sections with a per-file and total count. Each mention shows the exact line, and clicking it jumps straight there. A small count sits next to Pin in the note header whenever a note has backlinks.
  • Tags. Write a hashtag word anywhere and it renders as a subtle pill; typing the hash suggests tags you already use. Click a tag to find every note that has it. In Browse Notes, start a search with "tag:" to pick from your tags, then see each note with the exact lines the tag appears on — click a line to jump to it.
  • Browse Notes finds the right note first. Search now ranks title matches above body text, and both above notes that only mention your words inside a wiki-link — so searching "report" surfaces the note titled Report before one that merely links to it. Folder view gained keyboard navigation: arrow keys open and close folders and step in and out of them, and folders auto-expand to show matches while you search.
  • The editor adopts your Mac's accent color. Links, list bullets, the text cursor, and the quote bar all pick up your system accent instead of a fixed blue, and follow along the moment you change it.
  • Smoother scrolling with lots of images. Image-heavy notes used to stutter and sometimes jump to the bottom while scrolling. Images are now thumbnailed and cached, and revisited ones load lazily, so long notes stay smooth.

Bug Fixes

  • The global show/hide shortcut is reliable again. It could quietly go dead while the menu-bar toggle kept working. The real causes — a stale hotkey registration and a leftover duplicate app instance — are fixed, and the menu label always matches the real state now.
  • Switching notes is seamless. No more flash of the previous note's body, and no blank gap, when you open a note — the content swaps in a single step. A note you open also starts scrolled to the top, and the spacing under the title is correct from the very first render instead of appearing only after you scroll.
  • Focus lands somewhere sensible after you close a window. Closing one note window now hands focus to another open one instead of dropping out of the app and making you click back in.
  • The toggle behaves with several windows open. Showing again focuses the window you used last, never resurrects windows you deliberately closed, and no longer gets stuck when a note had a panel open.
  • Folder view is fast. Browse Notes crawled with folder view turned on; it's now as quick as the flat list.
  • Move to Trash works when selecting multiple notes. The Trash button in the selection toolbar did nothing — it now confirms and moves the whole selection to the Trash.
  • Enter accepts the suggestion inside lists. With the wiki-link or tag popover open, pressing Enter used to start a new bullet or checkbox; it now accepts the highlighted suggestion, even inside a list.
  • Editing a linked note's display text no longer corrupts the link, the picker no longer slides under the note title, and clicking a tag filters Browse Notes on the first try instead of the second.

item.title: Version 1.3.3
item.description:
• Exported HTML keeps your images. Image links used to point at files on your Mac, so they broke as soon as the file left it. Images are now embedded into the export itself, the file is a proper standalone page with your note title at the top, and Copy Note As HTML carries its images along too.
  • Click an image to see it full size. It opens in macOS Quick Look: zoom, pinch, close with Esc or Space. Web images open in your browser.
  • Nested lists line up. Every level steps in by the same amount whether you indent with tabs or spaces, and the focused line sits exactly where the rendered one does. We measured this pixel by pixel, five levels deep.
  • Reset Window Size keeps the window in place. It resizes around the center and stays on screen instead of drifting toward a corner.
  • The note header is a breadcrumb now. A slim row above the title holds the folder chip, Show in Finder right beside it, and Pin on the far right. Below that comes the title, then your text. The "Updated at" timestamp moved into the save dot's hover at the bottom right, next to the save status.
  • Buttons look clickable. The folder, Show in Finder, and Pin buttons show a pointing-hand cursor instead of the text cursor.
  • Show/Hide While Screen Sharing confirms itself. Toggling it shows a short toast with an eye icon: green for visible, red slashed for hidden.
  • Long titles use the whole titlebar. On a narrow window the title fills the space between the traffic lights and the buttons before it trims with an ellipsis.
  • Duplicate-shortcut protection works now. We announced it in v1.3.2, but a wiring mistake left it inactive in that build. Recording a combo that another action already uses gets a beep and a "Used by" note, and global hotkeys pause while you record so they don't fire mid-capture.

item.title: Version 1.3.2
item.description:
The privacy eye now tells you when it matters. The eye in the titlebar used to just mirror a setting. Now it shows up only while your screen is actually being recorded or shared, and it tells you where you stand: a red slashed eye means the notes window is hidden from whoever's watching, a plain gray eye means they can see it. Click it for a quick note on what's happening and the ⇧⌘H shortcut to flip it.

Long titles stay on one line. A note with a long title used to run its text under the toolbar buttons. Titles now trim to a single line with an ellipsis and stop short of the buttons.

The Action button (the bolt) is clickable again. With a long title the title label sat on top of the toolbar and ate clicks meant for the bolt, so its left half did nothing. Clicks now reach the button.

Shortcuts can't be stolen anymore. Recording a global shortcut that another action already uses is now rejected with a beep and a "Used by …" note, so you can't silently disable one hotkey by assigning its combo to something else.

item.title: Version 1.3.1
item.description:
Select a bunch of notes at once. Browse Notes now has a Select mode — tap the checkmark next to the sort button, or just Cmd-click any note. Tick the ones you want, then move them all to a folder (new folders included) or send them to the Trash in one go. Select All, Unselect All, and Done sit right there in the toolbar, and Esc backs you out.

Settings got a proper going-over. Global shortcuts now show as real keycaps — click one to record and it lights up the modifiers as you hold them, exactly like macOS System Settings, and Reset to Defaults puts them back if you change your mind. The Behavior switches are now sorted into Panel, Browse Notes, and System groups, each with an icon and a plain-English caption, and the Notes Directory row shows your folder, how many notes are in it, and a button to reveal it in Finder.

Smoother typing in big notes. The editor used to re-scan the whole document for code fences on every keystroke and scroll. Now it only looks at what's on screen, so long or code-heavy notes stay responsive.

No more phantom notes. When iCloud, Obsidian, or git touched your files, Flotnote could pile up duplicate or empty ghost notes and flicker the list. It now folds those bursts into a single refresh, only redraws when something actually changed, and drops the empty notes you've navigated away from — just like Apple Notes.

item.title: Version 1.3.0
item.description:
• New: **Action panel** (`Cmd+K` or the bolt button in the titlebar) — a searchable command palette with every Flotnote action: New/Duplicate/Browse/Find, Move to Folder, Pin, Show in Finder, Delete; Copy Note As Markdown/HTML/Plain Text (`Cmd+Shift+C`); Export to file or Share to other apps (`Cmd+Shift+E`); a Format sub-panel (`Cmd+Shift+,`) incl. new Code Block; Move Line Up/Down (`Ctrl+Cmd+↑/↓`); Reset Window Size (`Cmd+Shift+0`); Hide/Show Format Bar (`Opt+Cmd+,`); editor zoom (`Cmd+=` / `Cmd+-` / `Cmd+0`); and Show/Hide While Screen Sharing (`Cmd+Shift+H`). Copy/save show a success toast, Delete asks for confirmation, and shortcut badges reflect your configured Settings shortcuts. The Settings gear moved out of the titlebar into the Action panel (`Cmd+,` still works)
  • Much faster note search: results are now computed once per keystroke instead of dozens of times per render, sorting no longer happens while typing, and extending a query only re-scans the previous results — typing in Browse Notes stays smooth with large libraries

item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
• Fixed right-click menus (and their submenus) closing when the cursor moved outside the Flotnote window — the window's hover tracking no longer updates while a menu is open
  • New: folder picker in the title area — see and change which folder a note lives in; for a brand-new note it chooses where the file is created. Opens with a click or `Cmd+Shift+M`, has a search box to filter folders, and typing a name that doesn't exist offers Create "name" inline
  • New: right-click a note in the switcher → Move to Folder (also Pin, Show in Finder, Move to Trash)
  • New notes (Cmd+N / + button) are now created in the same folder as the currently active note instead of always the root
  • Renaming or moving a note no longer recreates the editor — notes now keep a stable internal identity when their file path changes, fixing focus hiccups after a title commit
  • Fixed rename filename-collision checks running against the root folder for notes inside subfolders
  • Fixed the entire formatting toolbar (Bold, Italic, lists, etc.) permanently stopping working — a stale cursor position cached from a previous note could point outside the current note; every toolbar action then failed silently, and the poisoned cache was never cleared until the app restarted. The cache is now invalidated on note switch and validated before use
  • Fixed tables sometimes not rendering when a note is first opened (only fixed by toggling Source Mode and back) — the table widget now rebuilds when background parsing finishes
  • Typing a single `-` under a line of text no longer turns it into a heading — setext H2 now requires at least `--`, so starting a bullet point doesn't restyle the text above. Note: `---` typed directly under text now renders as a divider (horizontal rule) instead of a heading
  • Fixed list lines jumping left when the cursor enters them — the active line now keeps the same hanging indent as its rendered version, and the raw `-`/`1.` marker sits in the same spot as the rendered bullet. This also makes multi-line selection highlights over lists align evenly

item.title: Version 1.1.5
item.description: • Fixed typing the letter "a" unexpectedly opening a file picker (or toggling the window) after a keyboard shortcut had been cleared in Settings — a cleared shortcut is no longer mistaken for the "a" key

item.title: Version 1.1.4
item.description: • Fixed new notes sometimes refusing keyboard input — after a character or two, typing would stop with a beep and focus could jump to the desktop/Finder. New notes now reliably keep keyboard focus in the title and editor.

item.title: Version 1.1.3
item.description:
• Fixed notes briefly showing as empty (or jumping to a random note) while iCloud is still syncing — the current note now stays open and a "Syncing from iCloud…" loading screen is shown until downloads finish
  • Fixed underscores inside words being treated as italic (e.g. `test_one_two` rendered as `testonetwo`) — intraword underscores are now kept literal, matching standard Markdown

item.title: Version 1.1.2
item.description: • Fixed licensed users being shown the "trial ended" lockout screen — caused by the background ticker misidentifying a licensed user's permanent "trial expired" state as an actual trial expiry event
